_why_this_file: The design decisions are encoded here rather than only in prose so that they are
diffable, hashable, and readable by the build scripts. This file is the
definition_version source for the provenance block stamped on every shareable
TREAT THIS AS A PROTOCOL, NOT A TUNING FILE. Changing a value here changes what
is being estimated. It is not the place to make a failing run pass. Every edit
should be a deliberate, reviewed commit that also bumps definition_version.

exposure._node_statistic_why: Time-weighted mean of delivered dose over the CRRT records charted inside each 24h node, with charted zero-dose intervals included in both numerator and denominator, and NO imputation for uncharted gaps. Formula: sum(dose_h) / n_charted_hours over the node. REASON 1, consistency with the exposure: this study's exposure is DELIVERED dose (see _prescribed_vs_delivered). Downtime is precisely what makes delivered dose fall below prescribed, so excluding zero-dose intervals would quietly revert the exposure to prescribed intensity. REASON 2, external precedent at the same institution: Quickfall et al., Blood Purif 2026;55:197-209 (references/Koyner_antibiotics_crrt.pdf) computes delivered CRRT dose from hourly effluent flow rates averaged within patient, retains short interruptions such as filter changes and procedures because they are genuinely delivered dose, and excludes gaps >=48h rather than zero-filling them. Within a 24h node a >=48h gap cannot occur, so their rule reduces to 'use what is charted'. SUPERSEDES the earlier windowed_median choice. That choice was justified by the archived MSM's charting-lag artefact, but the objection was measured 2026-08-18 and does not survive a 24h node: hour 0 medians 21.5 mL/kg/hr against 33.5 at every subsequent hour, yet spread over ~24 hourly values it moves the mean by only -0.63 (p95 3.71) versus -0.02 for the median. Bounded, and under a delivered-dose exposure a genuinely slower first hour is signal rather than noise. SENSITIVITY: rerun with the median, and rerun dropping hour 0.
exposure._denominator_caveat: A fixed delta is a different absolute effluent change in every patient, against a fluid-overloaded actual weight. Known to matter: actual-vs-IBW moves the >=30 share from 46% to 76%. Open question 4 in the findings.
exposure._prescribed_vs_delivered: This is DELIVERED dose. RENAL and ATN randomised PRESCRIPTION. A policy defined on delivered dose is not directly implementable; this is a stated limitation, and it is sharper for an intervention estimand than for an association.
exposure._node_statistic_measured: Coordinating site, node 0-24h, 2,144 blocks, 2026-08-18. CRRT charting is hourly and regular (p50 through p95 of the inter-record interval all 1.00h; only 2.0% of gaps exceed 2h), so the time-weighting is well defined and nearly reduces to a simple mean of hourly values. Time-weighted mean: median 33.4, p5 18.6, p95 67.7, max 143.8. Median statistic: median 34.4, max 161.3. Spearman correlation between the two is 0.974, so the dose-response ordering is essentially unchanged; this is a refinement, not a different study. Shiftable fraction at delta=5, floor=15 is 93.3% under the mean against 93.8% under the median, so positivity is not degraded. REJECTED VARIANT: treating uncharted gaps as downtime (denominator = available follow-up hours rather than charted hours). It requires block_discharge_dttm, which is defective: 51 blocks (2.4%) chart more CRRT hours than their discharge timestamp permits, producing doses up to 904 mL/kg/hr. Blocked on todo 2e. It also drops the shiftable fraction to 86.1%.
exposure._node_statistic_site_heterogeneity_RISK: The rule 'include charted zeros, do not impute uncharted gaps' is only as good as a site's downtime charting. At the coordinating site explicit zero-dose records are just 0.6% of the series while 23% of blocks have a gap >6h, so downtime is more often an absence than a charted zero, and the statistic will therefore overstate delivered dose to some degree. A site that charts downtime explicitly and a site that charts nothing will not be measuring the same quantity. MITIGATION: the federated export must carry, per site and per node, the share of node hours charted and the share of charted records at exactly zero, so this is visible in pooling rather than silent.

_node_statistic_sensitivity_LADDER.purpose: Charted-zero versus uncharted-gap is genuinely ambiguous in flowsheet data, so it is pre-specified as a BRACKET rather than a single choice. The three rungs bound the truth from opposite sides and the width of the bracket is itself a reportable per-site diagnostic. Added 2026-08-18 at the user's suggestion.
_node_statistic_sensitivity_LADDER.S1_primary: Denominator = charted hours only. Uncharted gaps excluded entirely. Reads as delivered dose WHILE CHARTED, and is an upper bound on delivered dose. This is the primary, and it is the rung consistent with Quickfall/Koyner, who exclude long gaps rather than zero-filling.
_node_statistic_sensitivity_LADDER.S2: Denominator = first-to-last charted hour inside the node. Gaps INSIDE the observed CRRT span count as downtime at dose 0. Reads as delivered dose OVER THE OBSERVED SPAN. Available now: unlike S3 it never touches block_discharge_dttm.
_node_statistic_sensitivity_LADDER.S3: Denominator = full node follow-up. All uncharted time counts as downtime. Lower bound on delivered dose. BLOCKED on todo 2e: 51 blocks (2.4%) chart more CRRT hours than block_discharge_dttm permits, which produced doses up to 904 mL/kg/hr. Add once 2e is repaired.
_node_statistic_sensitivity_LADDER.why_S1_and_not_S2_is_primary: Measured 2026-08-18, coordinating site, node 0-24h. Uncharted gaps are NOT random charting lapses: in-hospital mortality falls monotonically with gap length, 73.4% at 0h gap (n=987), 66.0% at 1-2h (n=592), 63.4% at 3-6h (n=361), 52.5% at >6h (n=204); Spearman(gap hours, mortality) = -0.131, p = 1.1e-9. Absence of charting therefore mostly IS downtime, and downtime mostly means the patient is recovering. That vindicates the substantive reading of S2 but disqualifies it as primary, because it pushes recovering patients to a low exposure value by construction and so loads the exposure with recovery status: S2 median falls to 17.9 in the >6h gap group against 29.3 under S1, and Spearman(dose, mortality) rises from +0.219 under S1 to +0.237 under S2. This is confounding by indication amplified by a measurement choice.
_node_statistic_sensitivity_LADDER.consequence_for_step_02_COVARIATES: REQUIREMENT, not a suggestion. Because the S1/S2 difference is driven by liberation and liberation tracks recovery, the time-varying covariate set L_t at each node MUST carry the predictors of CRRT liberation: urine output, vasopressor status and dose, fluid balance, and SOFA at the node. Without them S2 is confounded in a direction that is now known in advance. LMTP handles time-varying confounding only to the extent that L_t measures it.
_node_statistic_sensitivity_LADDER.agreement: 46.0% of blocks (987 of 2,144) have no uncharted gap in node 0-24h, so S1 and S2 are numerically identical for nearly half the cohort. Gap hours: p50 1, p75 3, p90 6, p95 9, max 20.
_node_statistic_sensitivity_LADDER.reporting: Report the primary estimate under S1 and the full delta ladder under S2 alongside it. Per site and per node, report the share of node hours charted and the share of charted records at exactly zero, so a site whose downtime charting differs is visible in pooling rather than silent.
_node_statistic_sensitivity_LADDER.open_alternative_to_bracketing: The bracket could be replaced by an actual discriminator. If a co-charted hourly stream such as vitals is present during a CRRT gap, the patient was being observed and the absence of a CRRT record is more likely genuine downtime than a charting lapse; if nothing at all is charted, the lapse reading is more likely. Not built. Would turn S1/S2 into a single imputed statistic. See todo 1c.

policy._formula: d(a) = a - delta   if a - delta >= floor;   a   otherwise
policy._critical: NEVER clamp to the floor. The lmtp package supplies no guard for this and will not warn. Clamping breaks the Assumption 5 invertibility condition. See fluid_ARDS/plans/lmtp_discussion.md S4.4 and S4.7.
policy._delta_ladder_why: The ladder IS the dose-response result; report all three rungs, not just the primary. delta=2.5 is universally clean (max binned density ratio 2.6-6.0, zero mass above ratio 10 at any site). delta=10 is the clinically vivid rung but is diluted at two low-dose sites (moves only 23% and 27% of patients) and unstable at the two tight-dosing sites (density ratios to 31.0, 17-70% of cohort above ratio 10). Keep it, with the honest caveat.
policy._floor_why: floor=20 collapses policy coverage to 4% and 11% at the two lowest-dose sites at delta=10, and to 33%/23% even at delta=2.5/5 at one of them. Sensitivity rung only, never primary.

time._tau_why: Retention at 48h is >=38% at every one of the ten sites. A fourth node at 72h is viable at most sites but thin at one (27%). Do not go past tau=4.
time._outcome_grid_why: Exposure runs to day 3 but follow-up runs to day 30. The outcome nodes must be coarsened or the T x T influence-function covariance becomes ill-conditioned at small sites. Verify lmtp v1.5.4 mechanics for tau_trt < tau_outcome before relying on this.

outcome._definition: In-hospital by construction: death is taken from discharge disposition (expired OR hospice), so post-discharge deaths are unobservable. Hospice counts as a death (2.7% at the coordinating site). death_dttm is missing for 37% of counted deaths and the last vital sign is the fallback timestamp, which can flip a patient across the 30-day boundary. ALL OF THIS MUST BE STATED EXPLICITLY IN ANY METHODS SECTION.
outcome._competing_event_how: Via the lmtp `compete` argument. Matches the existing Fine-Gray CIFs in the sibling pipeline's script 05.
outcome._event_time_why: The event time is the discharge that ended the encounter block, NOT clif_patient.death_dttm. death_dttm is 37% missing at the coordinating site and unreliable at others, so using it requires a fallback, which mixes two timestamp sources with different error profiles under one column name. Measured 2026-08-18: death_dttm with a discharge fallback puts 48 deaths BEFORE CRRT initiation, against 10 using the discharge time alone, with identical 30-day mortality (1,392 / 64.9%). 39 of those 48 came from death_dttm itself. The disposition already establishes that the patient died, so taking the timing from the same source keeps flag and timing consistent. This also matches existing consortium practice for morgue and hospice discharges. death_dttm is retained as a DIAGNOSTIC column: where both exist they differ by a median of -2.5h, and by more than 24h in 15 blocks.
outcome._hospice_counts_as_death: 39 blocks at the coordinating site, 2.7% of deaths. A hospice discharge is a transfer OUT of the hospital, not a death in it, so this is a definitional choice that MUST be stated explicitly.
outcome._residual_impossibility: 10 blocks carry a death timed before their CRRT initiation. Same blocks as the Stage 4 late-initiation warning: the contradiction is between the CRRT timestamp and the discharge timestamp in the source, and no choice of event time fixes it. See todo 2e.

estimation._why_sdr: Diaz's own applied choice. See fluid_ARDS/plans/lmtp_discussion.md S6.3 for the real tradeoff against TMLE.

site_admission._replaces: The `high-dose arm < 100 patients` convention used by the point-treatment analysis, which excluded two sites.
site_admission._why: Outcome-blind and pre-fit. It also readmits the two sites the old rule excluded: under an MTP their support is among the BEST in the consortium (1.3% and 0.4% unsupported; max density ratio 5.5 and 2.1). They are low-dose sites already near the floor, so they contribute little to the contrast, but excluding them was never the right description of that. This inversion is a reportable methodological point in its own right.
site_admission._threshold_todo: Not yet specified. Must be fixed and committed BEFORE any pooled effect is estimated under it.

cohort._definition_source_history: Originally planned as a verbatim vendoring of 00_cohort.py from CLIF-epidemiology-of-CRRT @ ee4774b. Changed 2026-08-16: that file is a converted Jupyter notebook (55 cells, ~900 lines of diagnostics, no callable API), and clifpy 0.4.9 already provides stitch_encounters, compute_sofa_polars, create_wide_dataset and apply_outlier_handling. Reimplemented lean on clifpy primitives instead.
cohort._must_reconcile:
The cohort is intended to match the sibling CJASN analysis. Two papers from the same consortium must not report two different Ns without a stated reason. Because the logic is reimplemented rather than copied, equality is a CLAIM TO BE TESTED, not a fact.

REFERENCE: the sibling pipeline's own STROBE output, CLIF-epidemiology-of-CRRT/output/final_no_phi/crrt_epi/{SITE}_strobe_counts.csv, which is regenerated whenever that pipeline runs. Do not hardcode a target here; read it from that file, so the comparison tracks the reference rather than a snapshot of it.

STANDING AT THE COORDINATING SITE (2026-08-18): this pipeline gives 2,144 blocks against the sibling's 2,145 (4_encounter_blocks_with_weight). One block of the difference is the documented ESRD-grain divergence in esrd_exclusion._known_divergence_from_sibling, where we implement the sibling's stated intent rather than its output. Any further divergence at any site should be explained before results are reported.

An earlier version of this field named 2,136 as the expected count. That figure was the UCMC row of the feasibility audit's tier-1 dose-percentile table, i.e. how many blocks appeared in one audit CSV built from an older vintage of the sibling's intermediate_phi. It was never a cohort definition and should not have been treated as a target.

substantially through 2020-2021. If each site contributed whatever range it
happened to hold, the pooled estimate would be over a mixture of calendar
periods, between-site heterogeneity would partly reflect WHEN each site
contributed rather than how it practises, and the Methods section could not
Inherited from the sibling CJASN analysis (STUDY_YEAR_START / STUDY_YEAR_END

cohort._stitch_why: Hospitalizations for the same patient separated by less than this gap are treated as one encounter block, the unit of analysis. 6 hours is clifpy's default and the sibling CJASN analysis uses it. PROTOCOL, not site config: two sites stitching at different intervals would be counting different things, and the ED-to-inpatient transfer pattern this exists to absorb is common everywhere.

esrd_exclusion._why: Pre-existing end-stage renal disease is excluded because the study is about CRRT for ACUTE kidney injury. A dialysis-dependent patient's CRRT is not treating AKI, and dose has a different meaning for them. PROTOCOL: the code list defines who is in the study, so it cannot vary by site.
esrd_exclusion._grain: Applied at ENCOUNTER BLOCK grain. If any hospitalization in a stitched block carries an ESRD code, the whole block is excluded; otherwise the partner hospitalization leaks back into the non-ESRD denominator. Pre-existing ESRD is a PATIENT fact, not a hospitalization fact.
esrd_exclusion._known_divergence_from_sibling: This yields 906 excluded / 2,246 remaining at the coordinating site, against the sibling pipeline's 905 / 2,247. Verified 2026-08-17: the difference is the single multi-hospitalization block, where the NON-CRRT partner carries the ESRD code. The sibling's comment states the intent we implement ('if ANY hospitalization in a stitched block has an ESRD code, the whole block is excluded'), but its diagnosis frame was narrowed to cohort hospitalizations before the ESRD lookup, so the partner's codes were never visible. We match their intent, not their output. Downstream reconciliation targets shift by 1 accordingly.
esrd_exclusion._code_normalization: Match on diagnosis_code lowercased with dots removed, so 'N18.6' and 'n186' both hit.
esrd_exclusion._poa_rule: Require present-on-admission, since the exclusion is for PRE-EXISTING disease. But if poa_present carries no positive values at all (some ETLs leave it unpopulated, e.g. the MIMIC conversion sets it to 0 on every row), the POA condition would silently exclude NOBODY and the cohort would just come out larger. In that case fall back to matching on code alone and say so loudly.

cohort._exclude_short_crrt_why: Dropped. It only ever existed because a point-treatment design needs 24h of therapy to define the exposure. LMTP handles early death structurally, so the exclusion is no longer motivated and would now induce selection.

_discontinuation_handling_RESOLVED.decision: CRRT liberation is neither a competing event nor censoring. It is an exposure value of zero, left unshifted by the policy.
_discontinuation_handling_RESOLVED.why_not_competing: A competing event is one that precludes the outcome. Liberation from CRRT does not preclude in-hospital death; liberated patients remain at risk and some die. The compete argument is correctly occupied by discharge alive, which does preclude in-hospital death.
_discontinuation_handling_RESOLVED.why_not_censoring: Censoring liberated patients would estimate the effect in a world where nobody is liberated within 72h, which is not the question asked. It would also break Assumption 1 positivity for recovering patients, whose probability of remaining on therapy approaches zero.
_discontinuation_handling_RESOLVED.why_safe: The self-limiting shift d(a) = a - delta if a - delta >= floor else a leaves zero unchanged, since 0 - delta < floor for every delta in the ladder. The policy can therefore never move a patient onto or off therapy, only change the intensity of therapy already being delivered. This is what makes dose = 0 an admissible exposure value rather than a covert 'dose or no dose' contrast.
_discontinuation_handling_RESOLVED.supersedes: The carry_forward_zero option was previously annotated as silently changing the estimand to 'dose or no dose'. That concern applies to a shift that could push a nonzero dose to zero or lift a zero to nonzero. The self-limiting shift does neither, so the concern does not apply here.
_discontinuation_handling_RESOLVED.interaction_with_node_statistic: Follows directly: a charted zero-dose interval enters the time-weighted mean at zero, pulling the node value down, which is the correct behaviour for a delivered-dose exposure. An uncharted gap does not enter at all. Decided once for all zero-dose intervals regardless of cause: liberation, SCUF-only intervals, machine downtime, filter clotting.
_discontinuation_handling_RESOLVED.sources_read: Diaz, Williams, Hoffman, Schenck, JASA 2023, pp.1-6 (vector-valued exposure A_t = (A_1t, A_2t) with censoring intervened to 1, p.850; Assumption 1). lmtp R package manual v1.5.4, pp.1-8 and 12-15 (cens mandatory for survival outcomes; compete separate and only for outcome_type='survival'). NOT AVAILABLE in the references folder: Young et al. 2020 and Diaz, Hoffman, Hejazi 2023, both of which bear on competing risks; read them before the competing-event framing is finalised in the manuscript.
_discontinuation_handling_RESOLVED.scuf_within_the_window: FULLY RESOLVED 2026-08-18. The cohort script no longer filters by modality at all: a row counts as delivering therapy if any dose-eligible flow is present and positive, which SCUF can never satisfy (verified: 0 of 4,660 SCUF rows have one). So SCUF needs no special case, and a SCUF interval is simply an interval at dose 0. The self-limiting shift already leaves dose 0 unchanged, since 0 - delta < floor. The node statistic now answers the remaining question: the time-weighted mean INCLUDES charted zeros, giving 'clearance delivered over the interval'. Note the mean does not share the median's pathology of returning a value never received: mean([30,30,0,0]) = 15 is the genuine average delivery rate over those four hours. Measured 2026-08-17: 128 of 2,246 blocks (5.7%) have SCUF inside their 0-72h window, median 2 rows, max 66. This is the SAME question as a dose gap from liberation, machine downtime, or filter clotting, so decide it once for all zero-dose intervals rather than per cause.
_discontinuation_handling_RESOLVED.scuf_before_t0: Related but separate. 342 blocks have SCUF plus another mode and are retained; only 3 blocks that are SCUF for their entire record are dropped. For those 342 the index event is the first DOSE-ELIGIBLE record, so t=0 sits later than the first CRRT record by a median of 0.6h, but by more than 24h for 18 blocks and by 61 days in one case. Defensible, since SCUF for volume overload and CVVHD for AKI clearance are different therapies for different indications, but it should be a stated choice rather than a side effect of filter placement.
_discontinuation_handling_RESOLVED._coverage_consequence: Treating zero-dose intervals as dose 0 rather than excluding them INCREASES the unshifted fraction, because the self-limiting shift leaves anything below floor+delta untouched (below 20 at delta=5, floor=15). Coverage is the estimand-dilution risk the feasibility audit flags as a headline diagnostic, so report the shifted fraction with the zero-dose intervals included.
